inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average, FY2026 10-K EPS note (494,588,254 shares; file:8400). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows and is immaterial (~0.28% of revenue) for this ASX industrial, so no dilution risk to double-charge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, Note 4 cash-flow reconciliation / remuneration note (file:7480); no separate equity-award-tax withholding line disclosed (SBC-zero-adjacent ASX filer)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:52:12Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range A$18.26-A$24.27, price near the 52-week low
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD CAPM: rf ~4.3% (AU 10yr), ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.75-0.85 (defensive, largely non-discretionary, government-payor-funded diagnostics; comparable low-cyclicality ASX healthcare names run 9-10.5%). Cost of equity ~8.4-9.0%; blended with ~26% net-debt/EV at an after-tax cost of debt ~4.1% gives WACC ~7.3%. Set base WACC 7.3%, reflecting a defensive earnings base but LOWER than a pure defensive due to rising leverage (gearing 9.7%->25.9% since FY2022, net debt ~4x since FY2022 largely LADR-funded, debt cover 2.2x, interest cover 10.0x). Risk differentiation between scenarios lives mainly in the flows (US turnaround, Swiss/NHS execution, M&A outcomes), not stacked again in WACC: bear 8.0%, bull 6.6%, a modest +/-0.7pp band.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost (principal + interest, both from the FY2026 cash-flow statement: principal AUD432.732m financing outflow, finance charges on capitalised leases AUD75.309m per Note 4, file:6054) is deducted inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (AUD2,121.4m FY2026) are EXCLUDED from net_debt/total_debt, matching Sonic's own covenant convention -- the company's own Net Debt to EBITDA and Gearing ratios explicitly exclude AASB16 lease liabilities (file:8567, file:8572-8575: 'Net interest-bearing debt excludes lease liabilities under AASB 16'). da_pct_path uses D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2026: total depreciation 771.498 less ROU depreciation 441.309 = 330.189, plus amortisation of intangibles 97.548 = 427.737, i.e. 3.94% of revenue) to avoid double-charging the ROU asset once via the lease-cost line and again via full D&A.
inputs.nci_treatment: Minority interests are material but small relative to group scale (~4-5% of pre-NCI NPAT: FY2026 NCI profit share AUD28.029m on pre-NCI NPAT of AUD636.322m). Folded into a combined cash-tax-rate-plus-NCI-leakage driver (cash_tax_rate_path ~26.5% base = ~23% underlying cash tax + ~3.5pp NCI leakage) rather than a separate bridge deduction, per the adaptations doc's 'fold the NCI profit share into a combined tax/leakage driver' option -- avoids a second driver line for a small, stable leakage rate. NCI dividends to minorities (AUD17.5m FY2026) are the actual cash leakage and are small (~1.2% of OCF).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF via the component-build engine (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing: standard non-US operating company, medical diagnostics/imaging -- owner-FCF DCF + owner-fcf-adaptations.md for currency/leases/NCI). Fresh build (no prior DCF/Drivers file existed for SHL.AX). Lease adjustment per financial-parser's note: reported FCF (OCF - capex) does NOT deduct IFRS-16 lease principal (~AUD0.4-0.5bn/yr since FY2020), so it is materially overstated; corrected via treatment (B) as above. FY2026 last_fcf of AUD131.7m reflects (a) the full lease-cost deduction and (b) a temporarily elevated capex run-rate (PPE capex 5.8% of revenue in FY2026 vs guided long-term maintenance capex of ~3.0-3.5%+~1.0-1.3% intangibles, driven by the Docklands hub (~AUD180m total, opening mid-CY2027) and Watford (UK NHS) builds) -- the forward capex path tapers to the guided maintenance level by year 4-5, so projected owner FCF margin rises well above the FY2026 actual as the capex supercycle rolls off. Currency: AUD statements against an AUD quote (ASX-listed, files in AUD) -- no FX conversion needed despite the diversified USD/EUR/GBP/CHF/PLN/NZD underlying operations (natural-hedged, translated to AUD for reporting).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blended judgment, not a single CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5yr EPS/equity CAGRs are negative/subdued because FY2021-22 comparators are COVID-testing-inflated (EBITDA peaked at AUD2.83bn FY2022 vs AUD1.88bn FY2026; COVID revenue fell from a AUD2.4bn FY2022 peak to just AUD62m FY2026) -- the 5yr figures describe COVID normalization, not the underlying business trend. The 3yr revenue CAGR (9.98%) is inflated the other way by the LADR/Cairo acquisitions (FY2026 revenue +13% total vs +5% organic). Owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful historically because FY2024-26 capex has been in a temporary supercycle (Docklands/Watford builds) that depresses reported FCF independent of the underlying earnings trend -- see inputs.notes. Base-case growth (5.5% decelerating to 2.7%) is therefore anchored to management's own disclosed organic growth rate (~5%) plus a modest, tapering allowance for bolt-on M&A, NOT to any single historical CAGR.

base.narrative: Organic growth settles around management's own disclosed ~5% (ageing populations, chronic disease, advanced diagnostics/genetics) tapering to 2.7% terminal as bolt-on M&A (Cairo-style, not LADR-scale) contributes a diminishing tail; no further transformational acquisition assumed. EBITDA margin recovers gradually from the FY2026 cyclical trough (17.3%) to ~18.8% as LADR synergies complete (>40% captured year one, more to come), the US cost-out program lands (AUD25-30m FY2027), and the UK NHS contract ramps by H2 FY2028 -- partly offset by the ~CHF20m Swiss fee cut. Capex tapers from the FY2026 supercycle peak (Docklands/Watford) to the guided ~4.3% maintenance level (3.0-3.5% PPE + ~1.0-1.3% intangibles) by year 4-5. Cash tax + NCI leakage held at a stable ~26.5%, consistent with the FY2025/26 actuals (21-23% cash tax plus ~3.5pp NCI).

bull.narrative: US operating review succeeds decisively (share gains against Quest/Labcorp beyond the guided AUD25-30m, not just cost-out), the UK NHS contract ramps on the original (not delayed) timetable so Watford margin accretion arrives by FY2027 rather than H2 FY2028, German consolidation into three unified divisions captures synergies faster than the LADR playbook implies, and advanced diagnostics/genetics (Sonic Genetics +15%, Biovis +12%, US Advanced Diagnostics +16%) keeps compounding at current rates. Further disciplined bolt-on M&A (Cairo-style) continues without releveraging beyond current gearing. Margin reaches a mature ~20.5%, well above the FY2019-22 pre-COVID range, reflecting full realisation of the scale/digital-transformation thesis.

bear.narrative: US remains a structurally weak #3 (~2% share vs Quest/Labcorp ~9% each) with the operating review failing to durably lift margins beyond the guided cost-out; the UK NHS contract integration slips further past H2 FY2028 as NHS operational issues persist, delaying the 15-year contract's margin payoff; Swiss and other reimbursement cuts recur and are only partly mitigated; LADR/Cairo integration disappoints on synergy capture; rising leverage (gearing already 25.9%, net debt ~4x since FY2022) constrains capital allocation and forces capex discipline that shows up as flat, not recovering, margins. No further margin-accretive M&A; growth settles near GDP-plus-ageing-demographics (~1.7% terminal), reflecting a mature, competitively pressured, no-re-rating base case.

scenario_narratives.base: Sonic executes its stated FY2027 plan roughly as guided: modest EBITDA growth (4-6% constant currency) as Swiss fee cuts and the delayed UK NHS ramp offset continuing organic growth, LADR synergy capture and the US cost-out program. Margin recovers gradually toward a mature ~18.8% as the capex supercycle (Docklands, Watford) rolls off toward guided maintenance levels. No further transformational (LADR-scale) acquisition is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: The US turnaround, UK NHS ramp and German consolidation all land ahead of the guided timetable, advanced-diagnostics growth keeps compounding at current double-digit rates, and margin reaches a mature ~20.5% -- above the pre-COVID range -- without further releveraging.
scenario_narratives.bear: The US stays structurally weak, the UK NHS contract slips further, Swiss/regulatory fee pressure recurs, and rising leverage (gearing already 25.9%, net debt ~4x FY2022) constrains capital allocation, holding margin flat at a depressed ~16.2% with no re-rating catalyst.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 shifted to 25/50/25: bear weight raised above default because leverage has risen materially and concretely since FY2022 (gearing 9.7%->25.9%, net debt ~4x, largely LADR-funded) even though it remains investment-grade (debt cover 2.2x, interest cover 10.0x) -- a fixed-income-style risk that a pure operating-risk bear case understates; also because the FY2027 guidance itself already disappointed the market (stock down ~9-21% post-results, trading near 10-year lows), so a below-consensus outcome is a live, not merely theoretical, near-term risk. Bull weight trimmed from the 35% default to 25% because the bull case requires several largely independent things to go right at once (US turnaround, on-time NHS ramp, faster German synergy capture, no further releveraging) rather than one dominant catalyst.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sonic is a scaled, largely non-discretionary, government-payor-funded diagnostics and imaging business with genuine defensive characteristics (low-to-moderate cyclicality, structural ageing/chronic-disease demand tailwinds, market-leading positions in five of nine countries) trading near a 10-year low after FY2027 guidance disappointed on margin-recovery timing. The valuation case rests on whether the FY2026 capex supercycle (Docklands, Watford) genuinely rolls off toward the guided ~4.3% maintenance level, whether the LADR and US integration/cost-out programs deliver as guided, and whether the reported FCF -- which has never deducted the ~AUD0.4-0.5bn/yr IFRS-16 lease principal -- has been materially overstating the business's true owner cash generation, which this build corrects via the lease-cost-as-opex treatment.
key_risks_to_valuation: Rising leverage (gearing 9.7%->25.9% since FY2022, net debt ~4x, largely LADR-funded) reduces balance-sheet flexibility just as rate sensitivity increases
US segment remains a distant, sub-scale #3 with near-flat organic growth and an unproven multi-year operating review
UK NHS contract margin timing has already slipped once (to H2 FY2028) and could slip again given ongoing NHS operational issues
Regulatory/reimbursement risk is concrete and near-term (Swiss fee cuts ~CHF20m FY2027, PBS/Medicare and PAMA pressure ongoing)
Growth strategy remains acquisition-dependent, carrying integration and synergy-realisation risk across a federated multi-country model
High dividend payout ratio (87.7% FY2026, 101.8% FY2025) leaves limited buffer if earnings growth disappoints again
